channel.title: Morning Briefing – Macro & Europe
channel.description: Private daily macro and European equities briefing
channel.itunes:author: Morning Briefing

item.title: Briefing – Friday, 20 November 2026
item.description: - Thesis: AI sell-off becomes global de-risking. Anthropic IPO up seventeen percent on day one, yet Nasdaq 100 down two point two percent and S&P 500 down two percent. - Trigger chain: Huang resignation, subpoena, Nvidia down 669 billion dollars in six days, AMD down over seven percent, Intuit weak outlook. - Asia: Kospi down five point seven percent, Nikkei down four point seven, Hang Seng down two point one. SoftBank down over sixteen percent. Worst week since 2020. - Rates and FX: US ten-year at five point one percent, dollar near 19-month high, Japan core inflation up and rate-hike expectations firm. Bund ten-year at three point four percent. - Commodities: gold down four point five percent, copper down two point eight percent and ten percent on the week, Brent at ninety dollars. - VIX at twenty-eight point four, up fifty-two percent in five days. - Walmart: EPS 0.65 vs 0.64 estimate, outlook raised, diesel cost hit of 2 billion dollars, stock down about one percent. - Model (rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about minus 105 basis points. Telecom, utilities, healthcare, real estate favored; tech, industrials, resources, luxury lag.

item.title: Briefing – Thursday, 19 November 2026
item.description: - Thesis: hawkish Fed (Waller half-point talk, Barr) plus AI wobble squeezes risk. US 10-year at 5.1 percent, VIX 24.6, up 40 percent in five days. - Nvidia fell after earnings on CEO exit and succession, China and export-control worries, dragging CoreWeave and Iren. Microsoft down nearly 9 percent from its record. - Anthropic IPO over 81 billion dollars, with a muted Asian reaction. AI debt hedging is building. - Palo Alto raised its outlook and bought Applied Compute for 4.5 billion dollars, showing demand in AI security. - Consumer: Target, TJX and Lowe's strong. Walmart reports today. - Brent 89.3 dollars, down 2.9 percent. TTF down 5.3 percent. Copper down 8 percent over 5 days. Iran strike reports are an oil risk. - Bund 10-year 3.41 percent, up 2 basis points. EUR/USD about 1.10. Dollar near a 19-month high. - Model (historical, Hang Seng-driven): Stoxx 600 about minus 23 basis points. Commodities minus 40, luxury minus 37, tech minus 15, utilities plus 19, telecom plus 10 versus market.

item.title: Briefing – Wednesday, 18 November 2026
item.description: - Nvidia: EPS 2.68 vs 2.47 (+8.4%), guide about 130bn dollars, stock about minus 0.4% as CEO exit, SEC probe and governance dominate. - Kress: "disciplined" financing of neoclouds, so circular AI funding worries persist. Congress pushes China chip export curbs. - Rates: US 10-year about 5.1%, Fed's Williams sees more hikes, BofA flags a possible 50bp hike in December. Dollar near 19-month high. - Oil shock: Brent about 93 dollars, Iran strikes in Kuwait and Bahrain, Hormuz standoff. Chain: oil, then inflation, then yields, then funding costs for small and mid caps, then capex. - VIX 25.5 (+11% on day, +31% over five days). S&P minus 1.0%, Nasdaq 100 minus 0.7%. - Europe yesterday: Euro Stoxx 50 minus 2.2%, DAX minus 2.1%, Stoxx 600 minus 1.8%. Bund 10-year about 3.4%. - Model (rule of thumb, R-squared 0.22 for the Stoxx 600): Stoxx 600 about minus 20bp, luxury versus market about minus 30bp, resources versus market about plus 4bp. - Watch: Trump, Xi and Putin in Shenzhen, Anthropic IPO on Nov 19, Gulf escalation, Target earnings.

item.title: Briefing – Tuesday, 17 November 2026
item.description: - Thesis: AI jitters plus hawkish rates plus a strong dollar. Bonds are not offering their usual cushion. - Wall Street Monday: S&P 500 down 1.9 percent, Nasdaq 100 down 2.7 percent, VIX up 18.7 percent to 22.9. - Asia: Kospi down 2.0 percent (down 4.6 percent over five days), ASX down 1.8, Nikkei down 1.1, Hang Seng down 0.7. - Rates: US ten-year at 5.12 percent, down 3.3 basis points. Bund ten-year 3.43 percent, up 2 basis points. RBA sees a fifth hike needed. - FX: Dollar at a 19-month high on Fed hike bets. EUR/USD 1.10, USD/JPY 159.1. - Commodities: Brent 91.6 dollars. Gulf tension (third US carrier) versus Q4 surplus forecasts. TTF down 6.8 percent. Gold and copper both down about 3.5 percent over five days. - Europe: Stoxx 600 down 0.3 percent Monday. Rule of thumb implies a lower open (about minus 57 basis points, R-squared 0.22). Energy relatively favored, resources lagging. - Catalysts: Disney results before the US open, Nvidia earnings this week (first since Huang's exit). No earnings data since yesterday.

item.title: Briefing – Monday, 16 November 2026
item.description: - Thesis: AI trade fragile into Nvidia earnings Tuesday, with high oil and rising yields leaving little cushion. - Asia: Kospi down 3.8 percent, Nikkei down 2.3 percent; Nasdaq futures down about 1.0 percent after Nasdaq 100 fell 1.2 percent Friday. - Rates: US ten-year 5.15 percent, up 5.1 basis points; Bund ten-year 3.41 percent, up 8 basis points. Higher discount rate hurts long-duration tech. - Japan: Q3 GDP contracted (annualized minus 0.1 percent) as energy subsidies expired; BOJ's Takata wants quick hikes. USD/JPY about 159.4. - China: October output, retail sales and investment missed; foreign reserve requirement hiked for the first time in five years. Copper down 4.8 percent over five days. - Oil: Brent 95.5 dollars; Iran rhetoric and the November 19 Shenzhen summit are two-way risks. - Sensitivity model (historical rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about minus 23 basis points, tech minus 29, industrials minus 25, healthcare plus 21, telecoms plus 21. Low R-squared. - Europe: Stoxx 600 up 2.4 percent on the week; tech and Asia-exposed industrials most at risk, healthcare and telecoms the tactical defensive.

item.title: Briefing – Friday, 13 November 2026
item.description: - Thesis: equities absorbed the Nvidia CEO resignation (stock down over four percent, S&P 500 down 0.3 percent, VIX 18.7), but rates are the bigger risk. - Rates chain: US 10-year up 10.5 basis points to 5.1 percent, 5-year up 11.8, on Fed hike expectations; biggest surge since 2022 per MarketWatch. - FX chain: higher yields lead to a stronger dollar, EUR/USD 1.106 (down 1.5 percent over 5 days), USD/JPY near 160, Japan's finance minister vows action. - Asia: Hang Seng down 1.2 percent, Kospi down 1.0, Nikkei up 0.6 (up 6.5 percent over 5 days). Chinese chip shares rallied on the Huang turmoil. - Earnings: Siemens EPS 3.01 vs 2.81 expected, stock up about 2 percent, record orders, buying Lauterbach. Allianz EPS 7.41 vs 8.17, stock flat. - AI split: Nebius down 16 percent on higher capex, Cerebras up 17 percent on Microsoft deal. - Sensitivity model (historical rule of thumb): real estate about minus 24 basis points vs market, commodities minus 20, luxury minus 2. - Watch: Trump-Xi summit next week, yen intervention risk, Fed commentary, Brent at $95.5.

item.title: Briefing – Thursday, 12 November 2026
item.description: - CoreWeave beat and raised guidance, stock up more than 24 percent, easing AI spending worries and lifting chips; VIX down about 10 percent to 17.5. - Nvidia down roughly 8 percent after hours on reports the board may oust Jensen Huang; Nasdaq futures down 1.1 percent, S&P futures down 0.5 percent. - Chain: Huang's opposition to export controls, U.S. probe into Megaspeed, and possible tighter China chip rules lead to semiconductor policy risk. Kospi down 1.3 percent, Hang Seng down 0.9 percent, Nikkei down 0.8 percent. - Hot October CPI and Fed hike talk: US 10-year at about 5.0 percent; oil-yield link has broken, so lower oil (Brent about 92 dollars, down 6.6 percent over 5 days) isn't lowering yields. - Bund 2-year up 7 basis points to 3.08 percent, 10-year up 6 basis points to 3.34 percent: higher funding costs for small and mid caps, capex risk. - Euro-dollar about 1.108, down 0.8 percent; USD/JPY near 160 with intervention warning and mixed BOJ signals. - Model (historical rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 plus 8 basis points, luxury minus 6, commodities minus 45 (low R-squared 0.09); futures point the other way. - Other: Nissan second forecast cut on China, Spain general strike, EU reportedly delaying EV tariff with Britain.

item.title: Briefing – Wednesday, 11 November 2026
item.description: - Hot October CPI (up 0.4 percent) pushed US 10-year yield up 11.9 basis points to about 4.98 percent; 5-year up 14.8 basis points. - Fed hike odds for December at 88 percent (CME FedWatch); Goldman sees another hike in March. - Asia bounced (Kospi up 2.1 percent, Nikkei up 1.2 percent), but Kospi is still down 5.9 percent over five days: oversold repair. - US futures up (S&P 0.7 percent, Nasdaq 1.4 percent) after Tuesday's small declines. - Brent around 92 dollars after briefly dipping below 90 on Iran peace hopes; US gasoline below 4 dollars. - Bund 10-year at 3.28 percent, down 2 basis points: widening US-Europe yield gap, EUR/USD down 0.5 percent to 1.12. - Model (rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about minus 6 basis points; real estate relative minus 22 basis points on higher US yields. - Infineon: EPS 0.60 vs 0.62 estimate (miss of 3.9 percent), stock up 6.3 percent on AI data center demand. CoreWeave beat and raised; Anthropic IPO range 70 to 78 dollars, trading expected Nov 19.

item.title: Briefing – Tuesday, 10 November 2026
item.description: - Core chain: Brent down about twelve percent in five days, now around ninety-one dollars, so lower inflation and margin pressure, so risk-on relief rally in Asia and the US. - Asia: Kospi up four point one percent, Nikkei up two point seven, but still down seven point six and four point three over five days. This is a bounce, not a trend. - Tension: US ten-year at four point nine percent, Bund ten-year at three point three, up three basis points, and the German two-year at three percent, up four. Bonds still price sticky inflation. - Today's key event: US consumer price report for October, expected to show slower price increases. It tests the rotation trade. - Nvidia and Huang affair: AMD and Broadcom gained, and the political and governance risk for AI is rising. VIX fell twenty-two percent to about twenty. - China exports up thirty-five percent, surplus above one trillion dollars. Supports volumes, adds trade friction. - UniCredit earnings per share two point one five euros versus one eighty-eight expected, a fourteen percent beat, but the stock is down half a percent. Banks may be crowded. - Rule of thumb: Stoxx 600 about half a percent higher, industrials stronger, telecom, utilities and energy weaker. Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi are a swing factor for defence.

item.title: Briefing – Monday, 9 November 2026
item.description: - Asia bounce: Nikkei up 2.7%, but still down 6.8% over five days; Kospi down 13.5% over five days. Looks like relief, not a trend change. - Oil: Brent at 97.5 dollars, down 7% on the week. Iran headlines remain the swing factor for inflation and margins. - China PPI 5.7% vs 5.3% expected, highest in over four years, while CPI cools. Input-cost squeeze with weak demand. - Rates: US 10-year 4.86%, up 2.2bp; US 5-year up 4bp. Bund 10-year 3.27%, down 4bp; 2-year 2.95%, down 6bp. - Europe Friday: DAX down 1.9%, Stoxx 600 down 1.0% with falling Bund yields, a growth-scare pattern. - Nvidia: board probe of CEO Huang over alleged Chinese spy link; shares fell after hours. Governance risk on a crowded AI trade. - Sensitivity model (rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about +40bp, tech +27bp and industrials +22bp relative; utilities -33bp, real estate -32bp, telecom -28bp. Mostly Nikkei-driven, low R-squared. - VIX 25.6, down 9% on the day but up 32% on the week; EUR/USD 1.12, USD/JPY 158.3.

item.title: Briefing – Friday, 6 November 2026
item.description: - Chain: Democratic midterm sweep, data center moratorium calls, AI capex doubt, Nasdaq 100 down 6.4%, S&P 500 down 4.4%, VIX 28.2 (up about 70%). - Asia as AI supply chain: Nikkei down 6.3%, Kospi down 4.9%, Hang Seng down 1.3%; headlines say Korea halted trading and Taiwan had its steepest fall ever. - Rates: US 10-year 4.84% (down 5.7bp), Bund 10-year 3.31% (down 4bp); yields fall on fear while Barkin signals gradual hikes. Growth and inflation worries coincide. - Oil: Brent $99.4, up 1.1% today but down 15.5% over five days; US-Iran risk could push it above $100. - Dollar bid: EUR/USD 1.12, down 0.3%. - Earnings: Deutsche Telekom EPS 0.63 vs 0.62, targets raised, buyback below forecasts, stock up 3.6%. Figma fell despite a beat; Cloudflare rebounded on its fastest sales growth in nearly four years. - Model (rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about -1.4% (R² 0.22). Telecom +79bp, utilities +77bp, oil and gas +69bp, real estate +50bp vs market; industrials -51bp, tech -49bp. - Risks: crowded defensive positioning, French budget rejection and strikes, S&P futures flat and Nasdaq futures up 0.8% hint at a bounce.

item.title: Briefing – Thursday, 5 November 2026
item.description: - Blue wave: divided Washington read as fewer policy shocks. S&P 500 up 1.6%, VIX down 20% to 16.6. - Oil: Brent below 90 on the day, now 94.2, down 18% in five days. Lower inflation pressure, US 10-year down 5.8bp to 4.9%. - AI doubt: Texas results hit data-center and power names. Kospi down 5.2%, Nikkei down 1.8%, Nasdaq futures down 1.3%. - Qualcomm down 7% on weak guidance (memory costs). Figma hit by AI delivery costs. AMD data center revenue nearly doubled. - Hang Seng up 3.3%, which drives the model's Europe read: Stoxx 600 around +19bp (rule of thumb, not a forecast). - Model: luxury +90bp, healthcare +51bp, autos +41bp; utilities -40bp, tech -39bp, oil and gas -15bp. - Earnings: BMW EPS beat 44%, stock down 1.8% on margin worries. Novo beat 18%, stock flat. - Watch: Bank of England hike, BOJ minutes, debt-ceiling standoff, Korea stabilization.

item.title: Briefing – Wednesday, 4 November 2026
item.description: - Democrats winning the Senate leads to a weaker dollar, with euro-dollar at 1.12, and a tech and AI data center policy risk, so futures are down (Nasdaq future minus 0.7 percent). - AI fundamentals remain strong (AMD up 8 percent, data center revenue nearly doubled; Super Micro up), but Apple and Shopify were punished, so the tape is less forgiving. - Meta is seeking up to 25 billion dollars in bonds, and the US ten-year yield is 4.95 percent (up 5.8 basis points), so the AI funding cost is rising. - Asia: Nikkei minus 2.6 percent, Kospi minus 1.0 percent and minus 7.0 percent over five days; China services growth at a three-month low. - Brent at 103.9 dollars (minus 10 percent over five days) amid Iran diplomacy hopes; high fuel costs hit margins (JetBlue); copper minus 4.3 percent over five days. - Bund 10-year at 3.35 percent and 2-year at 3.04 percent, little changed, so Europe is importing an equity shock rather than a rates shock. - Sensitivity model (historical, low R-squared): Stoxx 600 around minus 26 basis points; technology and industrials lag; utilities, real estate and telecoms tend to outperform. - Earnings: Intesa up 1.1 percent on record profit and raised guidance; Ferrari raised guidance; Schaeffler cutting 3,460 jobs. VIX at 20.8, up 19 percent in five days, which points to positioning.

item.title: Briefing – Tuesday, 3 November 2026
item.description: - Core chain: AI worries, Nasdaq 100 down 1.4% (down 4.4% over five days), Kospi down 3.9%. Memory crunch (DRAM prices doubled this year) hits Apple and device makers. - Apple: EPS 2.10 vs 1.99 expected (5.8% surprise), stock down about 1.8% on memory costs and slower services. - Palantir: commercial revenue up 148% to 984 million dollars, above government at 953 million. Stock fell on slower U.S. commercial contract growth. - Rates: US 10-year 4.89% (down 3.5 bp), Bund 10-year 3.34% (down 4 bp). VIX 21.2, up 8.9%. - Oil: Brent about 105 dollars after a 7%+ drop on Iran peace hopes. Qeshm Island strike keeps risk alive. TTF gas down 8.7%. Ryanair warns of fares up to 20%. - RBA hiked to an 18-year high (fifth hike this year) and raised inflation forecasts. China raised FX reserve requirement to 6% to slow the yuan's rally. - Sensitivity model (historical rule of thumb, low R-squared): Stoxx 600 about minus 28 bp, healthcare vs market plus 49 bp, utilities vs market minus 10 bp. - Watch: Iran talks and oil, US midterms, Nasdaq futures, crowding unwind in AI leaders.
